implemented_requirements.evidence: main.py → add_tx() calls tracker.add_transaction(kind='expense', ...); tracker.add_transaction creates Transaction and appends to self.transactions.
main.py → add_tx() called with kind='income' via MENU option 2; same path as expense.
main.py → list_tx() iterates over tracker.transactions and prints a formatted table.
main.py → monthly() calls tracker.monthly_summary(year, month) which returns rows, inc, exp, net; printed to user.
main.py → breakdown() uses tracker.category_breakdown() which aggregates expense amounts per category.
main.py → add_goal() reads name/target and calls tracker.add_goal(name, target).
main.py → contribute() reads goal name and amount, calls tracker.contribute(name, amount).
main.py → show_goals() iterates over tracker.goals and prints saved/target and progress percentage.
main.py → balance() prints tracker.balance() which is total_income - total_expenses.
storage.py → load() reads JSON into BudgetTracker.from_dict; save() writes tracker.to_dict() to the same file; main.py uses Storage at start and on exit.

critical_issues: None identified that prevent core functionality. Minor edge‑case: breakdown() would divide by zero if total expense amount were 0, but the function returns early when no categories exist.
judge.summary: The provided code implements a functional command‑line budget tracker covering expense/income entry, transaction listing, monthly summaries, category breakdowns, savings goals creation and contribution, balance reporting, and JSON persistence. All core features are present and the program can be executed without missing modules, yielding a pass.
